### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **79** documentable anchor(s).

**67** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 45 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 50 pages)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a55d71fbbcd147816a81c0c14f32c960382377e` — the merge of head `9fd173cc7aec94854539b2ac6399ee3ea9b86791` into base `fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a55d71fbbcd147816a81c0c14f32c960382377e && git checkout 8a55d71fbbcd147816a81c0c14f32c960382377e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df 9fd173cc7aec94854539b2ac6399ee3ea9b86791 && git checkout -B drift-repro fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df && git merge --no-ff 9fd173cc7aec94854539b2ac6399ee3ea9b86791

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fb94249af41b399dc4597a16fb4ba7bf5eec21df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位 ACCEPT · head `9fd173cc7aec94854539b2ac6399ee3ea9b86791`

#31739 PR-3b (`Fixes #31739`): the AI service account's lifecycle doors. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, changeset `patch`. The paths give no review face, so the seat reviewed it at TIER_DEFAULT. It is not governed.

- **The doors.** suspend, resume, set-owner, retire, revoke-key and restore-key are session-only, so an API key never reaches them, the account's own included, and an account cannot lift its own stop or touch its keys. A person's id answers as unknown.
  - The owner (only while a member of the account's organization) may suspend, revoke and restore.
  - Resume, set-owner and retire are an organization or platform administrator's.
  - A retired account (no membership) is reached by a platform administrator only.
- **The seat's should-fix 1, done: a platform administrator's stop stays theirs.** Suspend never rewrites a ban already in force and writes a reason this family owns ("AI service account suspended", optionally with ": " and the caller's words). Resume by anyone but a platform administrator lifts only this family's ban (that mark, or the owner-left reason); any other ban answers 403. Pinned: after a platform-admin ban, an org-admin resume gets 403 and the account stays banned, while a platform admin lifts it; an owner's suspend leaves an existing reason unchanged; and the CONTROL, an org admin resuming its family's suspension, holds.
- **The seat's should-fix 2, done: retire reads the keys inside its unit of work, after the membership delete.** A key minted mid-retire is revoked, pinned with a hook that inserts one inside the transaction.
- **Owner leaves.** The trigger on `sys_member` (delete, and an update that moves the organization) suspends the departed owner's accounts in that organization only, keeps a stop already in place, and logs loudly on failure. Resume refuses (409) until an administrator names a new owner. set-owner does not resume.
- **Keys.** revoke-key and restore-key follow the restore guard's rules in the door: a membership-ended key is never restored, an administrator-stopped key is restored by a platform administrator only, a platform administrator's revoke with no reason records `administrator_suspended`, an existing reason is kept, and a restore clears it.
- **Accepted as-is:** retire overwrites an existing `revoked_reason` with `organization_membership_ended`. Retire is terminal and this only makes restore stricter, as the body says. Retire's rollback rides `engine.transaction`, as 3a's registration does.
- **Evidence (thread report):**
  - 22 of 22 ablations went red and were restored, 5 of them new.
  - The lifecycle and ledger conformance tests pass (38), as do both service-account dogfood files (13).
  - The plugin-auth suite and test-typecheck were green on d0e1eef3.
  - eslint, engine-double-contract, census, auth-mount-ledger and route-spelling are green on this head.

Landing: once CI is all green, check K, then relay `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
